priorities.finding: Request-context fields (tab, hour, weekday) are the only prioritized training-only feature group, with +0.00221 primary lift, full coverage, and positive lift on all four temporal holdout dates. Its warm user-and-item segment has GAUC 0.6312 and nDCG@5 0.5076; cold-user results are also usable (GAUC 0.6536, nDCG@5 0.4921).
priorities.recommended_action: Allocate the remaining budget to a narrowly scoped request-context implementation and confirm gains with a post-score, within-user ranking evaluation. Keep the feature set limited to tab, hour, and weekday; early-stop if the replicated temporal holdout does not retain positive GAUC and nDCG@5 movement.

avoid: Reject user_profile, historical_user_author_affinity, upload_recency, content_duration, item_metadata, historical_author_response, and historical_item_response because each has non-positive training-only primary lift.

Do not use current-impression outcome fields from the log sources, including long_view, play_time_ms, is_click, is_like, is_follow, comments, or stay-time fields; they are unavailable at ranking time.
Do not use video_features_statistic_pure.csv aggregate snapshot fields because their per-impression availability timestamp is not established.
Do not draw a cold-item conclusion from the reported segment: it contains only 8 rows and has GAUC 0.5 and nDCG@5 0.25, so it is too small for stable ranking or top-five diagnosis.
metric_diagnosis: The available evidence supports only a small, temporally consistent request-context gain. Warm traffic provides the most credible ranking signal because of its 84,937 rows and GAUC 0.6312, while nDCG@5 is modest at 0.5076, indicating that any benefit should be verified specifically at the top five rather than inferred from GAUC alone. No weakest-segment evidence was supplied, so there is no supported post-score segment-specific intervention beyond monitoring cold users separately and treating cold-item metrics as underpowered.
